chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd Allah ibn al-Walid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The first to enter Paradise will be Al-Ma'ruf and its people, and the first to arrive at my Basin (al-Hawd) will be [them].'

key_terms.الْحَوْضَ: Al-Hawd: The Basin of the Prophet Muhammad, a reservoir in Paradise from which believers will drink on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.الْمَعْرُوفُ: Al-Ma'ruf: The act of kindness, doing good, or benevolence

ai.seo_question: Who are the first to enter Paradise and meet the Prophet at the Basin?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith establishes 'Al-Ma'ruf' not merely as social courtesy but as a comprehensive spiritual practice encompassing both divine obedience and interpersonal benevolence, a concept central to Shia ethical theology. It links this virtue directly to eschatological rewards, promising precedence in entering Paradise and being the first to drink from the Prophet’s Basin (al-Hawd), thereby affirming the intercessory role of righteous deeds in the afterlife.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Al Waleed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The first one to enter the Paradise would be the (performers) of the act of kindness and its deserving ones, and they would be first ones to return to me at the Fountain’.
en.sarwar: 11. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Walid who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘
The first ones entering Paradise are those who actuate Benevolent Assistance and come to me at the pond in Paradise.’”
